$schema_note: files/plan.md Step 12.1. Each entry: { id, query, expected_answer, employer_id, policy_type, difficulty, category }. `employer_id` holds the employer's stable slug (e.g. "northwind-traders", matching scripts/seed_data.py's `_slugify(company_name)` and scripts/generate_synthetic_docs.py's folder names) rather than a database UUID, or null for a query that intentionally spans multiple employers or none in particular -- seed_data.py assigns employer UUIDs randomly at seed time, so a fixed UUID can't be checked into a static dataset. eval/run_eval.py (Step 12.2) resolves a slug to the real employer row via EmployerRepository.list_all() + _slugify(employer.name) at evaluation time. `policy_type` is one of PolicyType's values (health/dental/vision/life/disability) or null for employer-wide/off-topic queries. `category` mirrors plan.md's five named coverage areas for per-category RAGAS reporting. Every fact in `expected_answer` is grounded in the real, LLM-generated documents under data/synthetic/ (Step 11.2) -- including several genuine cross-document numeric inconsistencies in that synthetic corpus, which are used deliberately as edge_case entries rather than smoothed over.
